title: Burler: no cluster-exclude warning when the profile has no cluster fan
brief: Every Burler round WARNs about dropped cluster excludes; fix at the source (#278)
body:
Repro: any loom run; every Burler round logs `shedadapters: focus directive names cluster excludes but the template profile has no cluster fan; dropping` (WARN).
Impact: the judge writes an `exclude_lenses` list nothing consumes, and the WARN buries real warnings in traces.

Found in crucible-happy-path round fable-high-r2.

Source: https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/278
Preferred fix: stop asking the Burler judge for exclude_lenses (and stop warning) when the template profile has no cluster fan, rather than only downgrading the log level.

title: A landed loom run marks its board task done
brief: A landed loom run marks its board task done
body:
Repro: `lyx board upsert` a task, `lyx fabric add <slug>`, `lyx loom start --no-attach` until `state: done` with the change landed on the parent; `lyx board get <slug>` still shows no status (no production code outside `boardcli` sets a board status).
Impact: the board keeps listing landed work as open and claimable, so the operator must `lyx board set-status` by hand after every landing.

Found in crucible-happy-path (round opus-medium-r1).

Source: https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/275 (close it in the landing commit).

title: lyx loom start pane layout: one-line status, no loom-operator, agent gets the height
brief: lyx loom start pane layout: one-line status, no loom-operator, agent gets the height
body:
Observed on the first real `lyx loom start` (go driver, task `burler-exclude-warn` in a loomyard hub), the task's tmux window holds four panes, top to bottom:

1. `lyx loom status --watch` — takes about a third of the window height. **Must be a one-line status strip**, as `docs/overview.md` already describes it ("a 1-line top pane").
2. `loom-operator`: an empty bash that `lyx loom start` adds (`operatorStrandAddSpec`, `internal/loomcli/bootstrap.go`, anchored `AnchorBelowParent`, so it lands directly under the status pane). **Must not exist.**
3. The producer agent (Discussion, then each later producer, each its own session) — the pane the work happens in. Gets only about a third of the window height; **must take all remaining height.**
4. **Selvage**, reed's permanent one-line shell band at the bottom (`internal/reedengine`, `selvagepane.go`). **This is exactly the operator terminal wanted** — keep it as is.

Wanted layout, top to bottom: one-line status, the agent pane filling everything else, Selvage.

## Why there are two operator shells

Both landed on 2026-09-19 from parallel work that was never reconciled: `d39b30648` replaced reed's header pane with a status line and Selvage, and `8ca2b9dbf` ("reed: born-as-strand for loom start's operator attach") added `loom-operator` as a separate tracked strand for the operator to attach in.
Selvage already is the operator's terminal, so `loom-operator` only duplicates it.

## Fix

- Stop adding `loom-operator`. If born-as-strand's tracking of the operator's pane is still needed (addressing, e.g. the mailbox design), make Selvage that tracked pane rather than adding another.
- Pin the status strand to one line.
- Size the agent pane to the rest.
- Check the same for the llm driver's layout, which adds a ly-drive strand.

Source: https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/279 (close it in the landing commit).

title: loom status shows the producer's stuck reason, not 'stuck with no OnStuck target'
brief: loom status shows the producer's stuck reason, not 'stuck with no OnStuck target'
body:
On the first real `lyx loom start` (task `burler-exclude-warn`, landing in PR mode), Publish created PR #280 and stopped to wait for review, which is correct. The status strand showed:

```
loom blocked | now Publish | last Publish → stuck | wait stuck with no OnStuck target
```

`stuck with no OnStuck target` is shed wiring jargon: it says how the recipe is connected, not what the run is doing. The producer's own reason was available — the trace carries `landingshed: producer stuck producer=Publish reason="pull request created; awaiting review"` and `landingshed: pull request created number=280` — but it never reaches `wait` in the status line or `error` in `lyx loom status`.

Wanted: when a row ends stuck with no OnStuck target, `wait` and `error` carry the producer's own stuck reason; Publish's reason includes the PR URL, e.g.

```
loom blocked | now Publish | last Publish → stuck | wait pull request created; awaiting review: https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/pull/280
```

This is the crucible-happy-path F7 residual ("the cause of a blocked row is visible only in the trace file"), now hit on a real run.

Source: https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/283 (close it in the landing commit).

title: Webster integration.md renders the verify command verbatim
brief: Webster integration.md renders the verify command verbatim
body:
On the first real lyx loom run (task `burler-exclude-warn`, PR #280), Webster's integration fork reported that the verify command in its rendered prompt `integration.md` was mangled by nested code fences, so it ran the plan's own `## verify:` command from `00-overview.md` instead.

The fork recovered by itself, but the integration stage's prompt carries the one command that decides whether the whole plan passes: a fork that trusts the rendered text runs something other than the plan's verify, and one that cannot recover it fails the stage.

Expected: the verify command renders into `integration.md` verbatim and unambiguous, whatever fences the plan's command or its surrounding prompt text use (e.g. a fence longer than any backtick run inside the command, or the command outside a fenced block).

Source: https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/285 (close it in the landing commit).
